## Writing and changing

Cell creation, targeted updates, documentation insertion, and examples.

Writing notebooks safely is harder than appending text to a file. A
notebook edit needs to preserve cell ids, clear stale outputs, validate
Python when possible, export through nbdev automatically, and avoid
overwriting the wrong cell.

[`write_nb`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#write_nb)
inserts cells; `replace_str` replaces literal text across notebook cell
sources.

There are two writing modes because notebook edits have two different
shapes. Use cell-block writes when adding or replacing structured cells,
and use literal replacement only for exact renames across existing
cells. Both paths stamp nbskill metadata and export affected notebooks
automatically when they have an nbdev export target.
[`write_literal_replacements`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#write_literal_replacements)
is the public literal-replacement API.

### Production contract

The writing tools are production core. They must preserve stable cell
ids where possible, clear stale outputs for changed cells, validate new
Python, export nbdev modules after source changes, support dry-run
review for broad replacements, and verify structured batch edits by
reading the notebook back.

## Writing cells

The write layer turns structured cell plans into valid notebook cells
and keeps the on-disk notebook in sync with its exported module.

#### Adding cells

[`write_nb`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#write_nb)
is the broad insertion tool. It can append, insert before or after a
stable cell id, replace a whole notebook, or write into a named chapter
while preserving notebook structure.

## Updating and splitting

Use one-cell updates for surgical changes; use explosion or chapter
splitting when the notebook structure itself is the thing being changed.

#### Updating one cell

[`update_cell`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#update_cell)
is the surgical tool. It keeps the original cell id, can replace a whole
cell or only a line range, clears stale outputs,.

For whole-cell replacement, pass exactly one notebook cell block:
optional `%%code`, `%%markdown`, or `%%raw` marker followed by the cell
source. Do not include standalone `---` separators; those mean multiple
cells and belong with
[`write_nb`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#write_nb)
or
[`batch_edit_nb`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#batch_edit_nb).
Use `line_range` or `old_str` when replacing only part of a cell.

[`update_cell`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#update_cell)
accepts exact Python text. MCP callers send structured source directly,
so no newline decoding or temporary patch files are needed.

#### Exploding function cells

[`explode_cell`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#explode_cell)
splits a code cell containing multiple top-level functions into one code
cell per function. The generated cells keep the original leading
directives, and the normal notebook commit path stamps ids and nbskill
metadata.

## Batch operations

Batch plans are useful when several related edits should be validated
and committed together.

#### Batch editing

Agents often need to change several notebook cells together.
[`batch_edit_nb`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#batch_edit_nb)
accepts a JSON edit plan, runs the same notebook-aware validation and
locking as the single-cell tools, and prints a compact diff before
writing. Use it when repeated shell calls would make multiline code or
dry-run diffs fragile.

#### Verified batch edits

Batch plans are useful when an agent already knows the exact notebook
edits it wants to make. They are also risky if the tool only says
“applied” without checking disk.
[`batch_edit_nb`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#batch_edit_nb)
now writes the notebooks, reads them back, and reports a verification
status plus before/after hashes for each operation.

<a
href="https://github.com/MorsCerta-crypto/nbskill/blob/main/nbskill/write.py#L697"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

#### Splitting one chapter

[`split_nb_chapter`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#split_nb_chapter)
moves one `##` chapter into a new nbdev notebook. It copies imports used
by the moved code, imports source-notebook definitions that the moved
chapter still references, and promotes referenced private source helpers
by dropping the leading underscore. It remains a Python API rather than
an MCP tool because splitting modules is a broad, deliberate refactor.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/MorsCerta-crypto/nbskill/blob/main/nbskill/write.py#L974"

## Moving cells between notebooks

[`move_cells`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#move_cells)
is the transfer boundary: it keeps full cells intact, derives imports
from their AST names, and rolls both files back when a normal commit
fails. A name turns the destination into a new chapter; without one,
moves stay inside one notebook.

<a
href="https://github.com/MorsCerta-crypto/nbskill/blob/main/nbskill/write.py#L1060"

``` python
plan_path = demo_path("batch_edit_plan.json")
try:
    with write_demo_notebook("batch_edit_target.ipynb") as nb_path:
        write_nb(str(nb_path), "%%code\nvalue = 1", replace=True)
        nb = read_nb(nb_path)
        cell = nb.cells[0]
        plan = {
            "operations": [
                {"op": "set_cell_source", "path": str(nb_path), "cell_id": cell.id, "source": "value = 2"},
                {"op": "insert_after_id", "path": str(nb_path), "cell_id": cell.id, "cells": "%%code\nassert value == 2"},
            ]
        }
        plan_path.write_text(json.dumps(plan), encoding="utf-8")
        batch_edit_nb(plan_file=str(plan_path), dry_run=True)
        out = StringIO()
        with redirect_stdout(out):
            batch_edit_nb(plan_file=str(plan_path), dry_run=False)
        applied = out.getvalue()
        print(applied, end="")
        nb = read_nb(nb_path)
        assert cell_source(nb.cells[0]) == "value = 2"
        assert "assert value == 2" in cell_source(nb.cells[1])
        assert "[verified]" in applied
        assert "->" in applied and "inserted id=" in applied
        print(f"verified {applied.count('[verified]')} batch edit records")
finally:
    remove_demo_path(plan_path)
```

The write APIs accept ordinary Python values; MCP exposes only the
bounded editing operations needed for agent workflows.
